title: Rearchitect host↔GPU pipeline for single-copy buffers, affinity-aware threadpool, and scheduler hints
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Background: Host-side CPU overhead is a dominant contributor to end-to-end prefill+decode latency at low-to-medium QPS for many customers. Current pipeline performs multiple host<>GPU copies (staging for kernel-friendly layout, KV cache roundtrips, and per-request allocations) and uses a shared global threadpool that sees contention during bursts and large batch assembly. This ticket rethinks the host↔GPU path to: (1) provide a single-copy fast path for common cases, (2) introduce affinity-aware per-device worker pools and backpressure to avoid threadpool thrashing, and (3) expose lightweight scheduler hints to the prefill/decode orchestrator and kernel selector so we pick kernels that reduce hostside transform costs.

Scope & Goals: Implement a pragmatic, incremental rearchitecture that can be rolled out behind a runtime feature flag and validated with microbenchmarks and customer traffic. Specific goals:
- Eliminate at least one host<>GPU memcpy per token on the hot path for autoregressive models served in the hosted and dedicated modes.
- Reduce host CPU cycles attributable to scheduling and copy operations by >=30% in representative workloads.
- Reduce tail (p95) end-to-end prefill+first-decode latency by >=15ms for common sequence lengths.
- Ensure compatibility with existing KV cache semantics and quantized kernel variants.

Approach & Design Notes:
- Single-copy fast path: Introduce a pinned, page-locked staging buffer pool per-GPU that kernels can directly read/write. Replace the allocate+memcpy pattern for prefill with buffer handles that are zero-copy when model layout and kernel support align. Fall back to staged memcpy for incompatible quant/layouts.
- Kernel selection integration: Extend kernel selector metadata so kernels advertise whether they support zero-copy I/O for a given tensor layout and quant format. Selector will prefer zero-copy-capable kernels when latency or CPU cost is prioritized by the route policy.
- Affinity-aware threadpool: Replace the global shared threadpool for host pipeline tasks with per-device pools that are CPU-affinitized to a pinned set of cores (configurable). Pools support token-bucket admission and cooperative yielding to avoid long-running tasks starving short latency work.
- Scheduler hints: Add lightweight hints (e.g., prefer_zero_copy, max_host_latency_ms) to the prefill/decode scheduler. Scheduler uses hints + kernel capabilities to choose between batch composition strategies (larger batches with copy vs smaller zero-copy batches).
- KV cache semantics: Maintain existing KV cache behavior; when zero-copy is used, ensure eviction and persistence semantics still produce identical token outputs. Add unit tests for cache border cases.

Acceptance Criteria (measurable):
- Microbenchmarks: single-request prefill+1decode p50 and p95 measured on benchmark rig show p95 improved by >=15ms, and host memcpy bytes reduced by >=50%.
- CPU utilization: host-side user CPU cycles (per-GPU) reduced by >=30% under steady-state synthetic workload (mixed seq lengths, 64-512 tokens).
- No correctness regressions: end-to-end model outputs for regression prompt set show <0.1% change in token distribution measures (BLEU / perplexity proxy) vs baseline.
- Rollout gating: feature flag allows per-tenant opt-in; monitored metrics (errors, latency, CPU) stable for 24h in canary before broader rollout.

Implementation Milestones:
1) Design doc + selector metadata schema (this ticket) — deliverable: design doc link + proto metadata. (owner: Liam)
2) Pinned staging buffer pool and allocation API; tests for fallback path. (owner: Runtime infra)
3) Kernel selector changes: advertise zero-copy capability and update selection heuristics. (owner: Kernel team)
4) Affinity threadpool implementation + config knobs. (owner: Scheduler)
5) Scheduler hints and prefill/decode integration. (owner: Orchestrator)
6) End-to-end integration tests and microbench harness. (owner: Benchmarking)
7) Canary rollout, monitoring dashboards, and post-rollout analysis. (owner: Observability)

Testing & Benchmarks:
- Microbench suite: prefill-only, decode-only, combined; sequence length sweep [16,64,128,256,512]; batch sizes [1,4,8]. Capture p50/p95/p99 latency, host memcpy bytes, CPU cycles, context switch rate.
- Compatibility tests: all supported quant formats and layouts; ensure fallback copy path is exercised and validated.
- Production canary: 2% traffic on dedicated pool, monitor errors, latency regressions, and per-tenant CPU over 48 hours.

Rollout Plan:
- Feature flag default OFF.
- Phase 1: internal canary (QA infra) — run 24h.
- Phase 2: limited customer canary (2 customers in dedicated mode) — run 48h.
- Phase 3: gradual ramp (10% → 50% → 100%) across dedicated pools over 2 weeks with rollback thresholds defined.

Metrics & Dashboards:
- New dashboard panels: host memcpy bytes/sec (per-GPU), host user CPU cycles/sec (per-GPU), prefill p95, prefill+decode p95, kernel zero-copy hit rate.
- Alerting: if prefill p95 increases by >10% or error rate >0.1% above baseline in canary window, auto-disable flag and page on-call.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Kernel incompatibility: mitigate by robust fallback path and conservative selector heuristics.
- Increased memory pressure from pinned buffers: enforce pool size limits and LRU eviction; measure host memory increase and cap per-host.
- Thread affinity misconfiguration causing starvation: expose config and default to conservative core sets; provide tooling to rebind at runtime.

Links & Artifacts:
- Design doc (draft): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Host+Zero+Copy+Pipeline
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6812
- Benchmark dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/dashboard/host-pipeline-rewrite

Notes: This ticket focuses on the host-side surface and scheduler integration; a follow-up ticket will implement GPU DMA offload for NVLINK/DMA peers if early results justify the added complexity.
